title: Adidas – predicting transaction value (mock exam 2023/24 & 2025/26)
text: You are the marketing manager of Adidas and build a predictive model of future consumption from historical purchase data.

Dependent variable: total transaction value of the most recent purchase (€). Independent variables: gender (male = 0, female = 1), age at transaction, channel (offline = 0, online = 1), duration (days between purchases), social (follower on social media: no = 0, yes = 1).
Y = β0 + β1·gender + β2·age + β3·channel + β4·duration + β5·social. The overall model has an R² of 65% and is statistically significant.

title: Margarine sales in 10 sales areas (lecture example)
text: A sales manager explains differences in margarine sales (packages per period) across 10 equally sized areas.

Simple regression: Sales = 39.534 + 18.881 · Visits.
Multiple regression: Sales = 144.482 + 10.487 · Visits + 0.664 · Marketing investment.
Observation no. 6: 102 salesman visits, marketing investment 1,500, observed sales 2,278 packages.

title: Monthly unit sales: price, SEM and social media (lecture example)
text: Twelve months of data: units sold per month, price per unit (€), spending on search engine marketing (SEM, €) and on social media campaigns (€). Three outlier months (7, 8, 9) suggest seasonal effects, so a seasonal dummy (b4) was added.
Units = b0 + b1·Price + b2·SEM + b3·Social media + b4·Season. R² = 0.99, adjusted R² = 0.98, F = 133.64 (p = 0.000).

title: Profit of 50 tech start-ups (lecture example)
text: Data on 50 start-ups located in New York, California and Florida: profit, marketing spend, administration spend and state. Location enters as dummy variables (baseline: Florida). R² = 0.61, adjusted R² = 0.58.
